newsitem.title: FRANCE: Explosion kills one, wounds 17 in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Explosion kills one, wounds 17 in Algeria.

text.p: A booby-trapped parcel exploded on Tuesday in the Algerian garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of the capital Algiers, killing one person and wounding 17, the security forces said.

Less than three hours before the explosion in central Blida, four Moslem guerrillas shot dead Algeria's top workers' union boss Abdelhak Benhamouda by the union headquarters in the heart of Algiers, according to an Algerian government statement.

Benhamouda's bodyguard was gunned down in the ambush and a warden at the union building was wounded, said the Algerian official news agency APS. Eyewitnesses said the three men were killed in a hail of gunfire.
The bombing and Benhamouda's killing came four days after President Liamine Zeroual vowed in a nationwide address his government would eradicate "terrorism" from the North African country.
In a statement on Tuesday evening, the security forces said a booby-trapped parcel exploded at 4 p.m. (1500 GMT) on Colonel Amirouche street in downtown Blida.
The statement did not say who caused the explosion in the town where Algeria's main military and paramilitary headquarters are located.
It was the first time in the country's five-year-civil strife that a parcel has been booby-trapped.
Moslem guerrillas usually use car bombs or home-made bombs in their campaign which has been stepped up in the first 19 days of the Moslem holy fasting month of Ramadan.
A bomb exploded in a market in Blida seven days ago killing eight and wounding 10, according to the government-controlled newspaper El Moudjahid.
At least 176 people have been killed since January 10, with some Algerian newspapers putting the figure at up to 250.
At least seven other bombs have exploded in Algiers and surrounding towns in the past 19 days, in addition to massacres of civilians in isolated hamlets around the Algerian capital.
Algeria's ruthless Armed Islamic Group (GIA) warned it would step up its attacks, arguing the holy month is more fit for their guerrilla campaign.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
